title: Howling Fjord
body: The Howling Fjord is the southeastern doorway to Northrend, a land of deep sea inlets, pine forest and sheer bluffs. It is the home of the vrykul, giants of whom there had been no sign for centuries and who have now woken in great numbers. The Dragonflayer clan makes war from Utgarde Keep and its villages, with proto-drakes in the air and harpoon guns on the cliffs, while the Winterskorn hold Skorn and Baleheim. The Scourge walks here too, its necromancers busy among the vrykul at Gjalerbron. Into this the Alliance has come by sea to Valgarde and up the western cliffs to Westguard Keep, and the Forsaken of the Royal Apothecary Society have built Vengeance Landing and New Agamand to test a plague of their own. The taunka of Camp Winterhoof prepare to leave for the north, tuskarr fish from Kamagua on the Isle of Spears, pirates prowl the southwestern reefs, and iron dwarves have seized the old dig sites on the eastern bluffs.

title: Valgarde
body: Valgarde is the Alliance port on Daggercap Bay, built with bare hands, blood and tears, as Vice Admiral Keller puts it. It is one of only two safe harbors the Alliance holds in Northrend, and with it runs the main supply line into the continent. The port has been on the defensive since the vrykul first struck it, and Dragonflayer raiders and their worgs still hammer at the gate while proto-drakes circle overhead. Within the walls the Explorers' League, the draenei seer Thoralius the Wise and Lord Irulon Trueblade of the Argent Crusade keep their posts.

parts.body: Lord Irulon was waiting for a sacred blade. Argent soldiers died in the Plaguelands to see it cleansed by the light of dawn, only for it to be hurled into a den of the fallen deep in the Utgarde Catacombs, guarded by the unmerciful dead. The envoy Ares the Oathbound, sent after it, did not live to carry it out. Lord Tirion Fordring himself is to wield it as the Crusade works toward Icecrown, and Irulon calls him their greatest hope.

title: Wyrmskull Village
body: North of Valgarde the Dragonflayer vrykul have made their home among the old ruins of Wyrmskull. Worgs prowl a pit at the heart of the village, harpooners man the docks by the longhouses, and in a cave beside the pit dwells the mystic Yanis, herald of Ingvar the Plunderer. The bodies of Valgarde's defenders lie where they fell. A bridge over the worg pit leads to the tunnel down into the Utgarde Catacombs, where the Dragonflayers set captives against their gladiators in the Ring of Judgement and dump the losers in the depths for Scourge necromancers to raise as ghouls.

title: Utgarde Keep
body: Utgarde Keep rises in the heart of the fjord, the stronghold from which the Dragonflayer vrykul make war. Its master is Ingvar the Plunderer, the champion these fearless giants esteem above all, and from its walls his raiders and proto-drake riders go out against Valgarde and Vengeance Landing alike, so that both towns would gladly see him dead. Beneath the keep run the Utgarde Catacombs, reached from Wyrmskull Village, and above it, at the top of the crag, lies Utgarde Pinnacle, the higher hall of the vrykul.

title: Nifflevar
body: Nifflevar stands on the bluffs northeast of Wyrmskull, a Dragonflayer village built around great harpoon guns. Most of the harpoon attacks on Alliance frigates in Daggercap Bay are launched from here, and Dragonflayer warriors, rune-seers and hunting hounds guard the heights. From nearby Ghostblade Post the Forsaken watch the village and wait for reinforcements from Vengeance Landing, meaning to take it before the Alliance can, while a Forsaken scribe frets that the vrykul learning kept here will burn with it.

parts.body: Payback came from the vrykul's own weapons. With Harpoon Master Yavus slain and a stolen harpoon control mechanism in hand, an Alliance gunner seized one of Nifflevar's guns and rained fire on Wyrmskull below, burning its longhouse, dockhouse and stores and cutting down many of its dragon riders.
sources: quest 11430 description and reward text (Yavus responsible for most attacks; slain)

parts.body: Lieutenant Icehammer then built a harpoon controller of his own and tested it on the gunner, who was flung from Nifflevar's largest gun all the way into Valgarde. Guard Captain Zorek called it insane, but word came soon after that Ingvar, the Dragonflayer leader, was furious.

Scribe Seguine of Ghostblade Post would not let vrykul learning burn with the village. Ahead of the Forsaken assault, the three sagas written by the bard Helgus were carried out of Nifflevar: the Saga of the Twins, the Saga of the Winter Curse and the Saga of the Val'kyr, and Seguine set to translating them.

title: Vengeance Landing
body: Vengeance Landing clings to the cliffs of the fjord's eastern shore, the Forsaken port in Northrend, reached by zeppelin from Tirisfal and joined to the land above by a great lift. High Executor Anselm commands it, and every soldier here has come for one reason: to see Arthas killed. Cannons guard the docks, bat handlers fly riders over the fjord, and the kennel keeper Pontius raises plaguehounds, since living dogs will no longer come near him. In its laboratory the Royal Apothecary Society works on the plague it has brought north for the Scourge, complaining that the strains sent from the Undercity keep failing.

title: The Derelict Strand
body: South of Vengeance Landing the Bleeding Vale runs down to the Derelict Strand, where survivors of Stormwind's North Fleet were driven ashore when the Forsaken destroyed their easternmost ships. Hungry, injured and poorly equipped, they have barricaded the beach behind cannons along its northern wall and fight with the fury of those who know they are going to die. Dark Ranger Lyana presses the siege from the vale, where Deathstalker Razael's meat wagons sit stuck in the frozen ground and the bodies of both sides lie heaped across the field.

title: Baleheim
body: Baleheim is a Winterskorn vrykul town in the hills west of Vengeance Landing, facing the Forsaken blockade at Balejar Watch beyond the lift. Its warriors come at the blockade without end, each screaming louder and swinging a bigger weapon than the last, and the abomination Sergeant Gorth holds the line against them. Champions such as Ulf the Bloodletter, Oric the Baleful and Gunnar Thorvardsson lead the charges, and from the town their leader, Bjorn Halgurdsson, rallies his people in the name of Queen Angerboda, promising that the val'kyr reward those who fight without fear.

parts.body: Bjorn would not leave his town, so Lydell's assassins laid an ambush to the northwest and gave him a reason to. He was a known hothead, and a crude insult in his own tongue about his mother sent him charging out after the one who read it, straight into the trap. He never saw it coming.

title: New Agamand
body: New Agamand is a Forsaken town in the western fjord and the home of the Society's plaguebringers, who handle the practical side of deploying the plague and keep far better equipment than the soldiers at Vengeance Landing. Chief Plaguebringer Harris runs its laboratory, Plaguebringer Tillinghast dreams of a plague for every creature that lives, and the abomination maker Hacksaw Jenny stitches together whatever parts come her way, though most are spoiled by the plagues around her. Deathguards keep watch, and a bat handler keeps his bats ready at the edge of town.

title: Halgrind
body: Halgrind was a Dragonflayer village until the Forsaken took it. Its chieftain, Thorvald, fled west to a camp of his own, and the apothecaries have made the place a proving ground, spraying the vrykul left behind with plague from great tanks for weeks on end. The vrykul refuse to drop dead. Plagued tribesmen, rune-casters and handlers stagger among the plaguebringers, while from the abandoned vrykul tower at Ember Spear, just to the west, an Alliance scout watches and is certain the Forsaken are up to no good.

title: Westguard Keep
body: Westguard Keep crowns the western cliffs of the fjord, commanded by the dwarf Captain Adams. Its cannons fire on Skorn to the east, and its crossbowmen, gryphon riders and engineers have more work than hands. A pirate blockade in the Shattered Straits below sank all the keep's ships, so Bombardier Petrov bombs the pirates from a goblin zeppelin shot down while ferrying for the Horde, whose owner, Harrowmeiser, complains that he is a prisoner. The Explorers' League shelters its people and pack mules here, and a garrison is being readied for Fort Wildervar in the north.

title: Ember Clutch
body: Southeast of Westguard Keep lies the Ember Clutch, a forest that has burned since the Alliance arrived, its blaze spreading by some magic of its own. Proto-drakes nest among the flames. The keep's soldiers fear the fire will surround them within weeks, but the Ember Clutch Ancients, who seek balance in all things, blame neither the drakes nor their whelps. The true culprits, they say, are the newly woken vrykul: the Dragonflayer handlers who keep a lair on the forest's south side under their master, Skeld Drakeson.

parts.body: Captain Adams ordered the eggs and whelps destroyed, and the enraged proto-drakes struck at the keep in return. Mage-Lieutenant Malister, who had argued against the order, saw no choice but to kill three of the beasts. He called them noble creatures and hoped the young drakes would not remember the Alliance's shameful deeds.

The Forsaken tried their plague here as well. Plaguebringer Tillinghast sprayed the eggs and lured a drake down to eat plagued meat, dreaming of a strain that would work on any creature. The whelps only glowed green, the drake failed to dissolve, and Tillinghast wept over his ruined dreams.

title: Whisper Gulch
body: Whisper Gulch, north of Westguard Keep, is where most of the Explorers' League went to dig, and something they found there drove them mad. The deranged explorers attack anyone who comes near, raving that they have learned the truth and that IT is coming, That Which Must Not Be Named. The ore of the gulch leaves a strange feeling in those who carry it, and a voice no one can place whispers that companions have turned traitor. Squeeg Idolhunter, once the explorers' boss, keeps to a cave in the northwest corner.

title: Steel Gate
body: Steel Gate is the Explorers' League's great excavation in the northwest of the fjord, a deep pit worked by excavators and archaeologists under Overseer Irena Stonemantle, who would like to finish and go home before the Rivenwood to the north grows any worse. Flying machines brought from Westguard Keep haul sacks of relics up to crane platforms and fight off the gargoyles that harry the site. Nearby, a small band of taunka watches the digging in anger: their Sage Mistwalker came following dreams of a wolf and believes the dwarves are carrying off artifacts of his people's past.

parts.body: Irena's betrothed, Explorer Jaren, went west to the Chillmere Coast after rumored artifacts and found the Scourge instead, turning murlocs into mur'ghouls with scourging crystals. A controller taken from one of the dead brought the crystals' shields down so they could be smashed, and Jaren sent his love back to Irena with word that he was safe.

title: The Rivenwood
body: The Rivenwood is a haunted forest north of Steel Gate. Riven widows, great spiders that keep their victims alive for their young, spin cocoons among the trees, darkclaw bats and Fanggore worgs hunt there, and gargoyles and the souls of vrykul drift through it. Something, most likely the Scourge, has agitated every creature in the wood. The taunka have learned to fear it: a hunting party that came this way with Sage Mistwalker lost most of its longrunners to the widows.

parts.body: In a cave on the wood's snowy northwestern edge the worg Ulfang lies trapped, and he has been calling out in the dreams of Sage Mistwalker and Watcher Moonleaf. To those who reach him in worg guise he tells how, at the last full moon, a strange white worg named Garwal came from the north and, with the help of Ulfang's own brothers, took his pack from him. There is something unnatural about Garwal, he says.

parts.body: Ulfang's treacherous brothers were hunted down, and with the eyes of the eagle Talonshrike his enemy could be seen at last. Garwal was no worg: confronted, he threw off his disguise and stood revealed as a worgen. Ulfang leads his pack again, though his friends were left puzzled that the creature had come south from the Grizzly Hills.

title: Skorn
body: Skorn is the Winterskorn fortress east of Westguard Keep and south of Camp Winterhoof, a place of towers lined with rune-casters, longhouses, barracks and, at the summit, a thane's lodge with a great pyre before it. Its strange giants have lately woken and begun to spread, threatening Westguard and the taunka of Camp Winterhoof alike, and the keep's cannons fire on it when they can. Those who have fought there warn that these vrykul can rise from the dead, a different undeath from the Scourge's, unless their bodies are carved apart.

parts.body: A dragonskin scroll found at Skorn showed a vrykul thane rising into the heavens among angelic figures, a dark shape looming behind. Father Levariol and Greatmother Ankha read it the same way: the vrykul may have a way to transcend death, at least the worthy among them, and the Winterskorn thane slain beside his pyre had proved himself unworthy.

title: Gjalerbron
body: Gjalerbron, its name spoken as if it began with Sh, is the great fortress of the vrykul in the north of the fjord, a forbidden place to the taunka. Cages line its paths, holding prisoners of every kind, and Scourge necrolords, wights and horrors move among the vrykul warriors and rune-casters. Beneath it, in the Waking Halls, rows of dormant vrykul stand waiting, and overhead the frost wyrm Glacion circles. At its northern end, the great chamber of the Winter's Terrace opens onto the slopes of Gjalerhorn.

title: Camp Winterhoof
body: Camp Winterhoof is a taunka post in the foothills of Gjalerhorn, near the border with the Grizzly Hills. From a distance the taunka look like tauren, but they are sturdier and shaggier, and among them trust is earned, not given. Chieftain Ashtotem has decided they must leave for safer lands to the north before the fjord grows any more dangerous. Until then the camp gathers hippogryph down for the trek, culls the elementals of the hills one last time and prepares a final yeti hunt, while Celea Frozenmane's wind riders watch the skies.

title: Fort Wildervar
body: Fort Wildervar stands in the snows of the far northeast, beyond Skorn and close to the border with the Grizzly Hills. It is being readied for the Alliance expeditionary force that will climb from here into the hills: craftsmen sew winter cloaks, miners dig ore for weapons and trappers bring in meat and furs, all dreading Captain Adams's temper should the vanguard find anything unready. Homesteaders have come to settle, scholars study the iron dwarves at Giants' Run, and a hippogryph whose feathers turn aside arrows circles over the fort.

parts.body: Seen through its own eyes by way of Researcher Aderan's feathered charm, the hippogryph the settlers call Steelfeather was found to keep a nest of hatchlings close to the fort. Their 'he' was a she all along, Gil Grisert conceded, and the fort and its new neighbor would get along just fine if Trapper Jethan would only stop trying to make a trophy of her.

title: The Frozen Glade
body: The Frozen Glade is the snowbound home of the frost nymphs, of whom the taunka have told tales for generations. Their queen forbids them to deal with outsiders, but the land is changing and many sisters are in danger, so Lurielle now welcomes visitors. A destructive force has turned the glade's ice elementals against the nymphs, the Vibrant Glade to the southwest has thawed and driven its sisters mad, and the Twisted Glade to the west has filled with thornvine creepers and poisonous spores seeded by keepers who turned black of soul.

parts.body: Keeper Witherleaf, the mightiest of the blacksouled keepers, has fallen, and with him the strongest of the powers raising horrors from the waters and soil of the Twisted Glade. Lurielle grieves for the keepers, who were once the sisters' brothers and closest friends, but for the first time she sees hope for the glades.

sources: quest 11312 description and reward text (tales told by the taunka for generations; forbidden by our queen)
quest 11314 description (Vibrant Glade thawed; sisters driven mad)
notes: Checked: verified. Writer: AREA 4051. Part 1 on DONE 11428.

title: Kamagua
body: Kamagua is the village of the Kalu'ak tuskarr on the Isle of Spears, off the fjord's southwestern coast, and Elder Atuik is its chieftain. The tuskarr live mostly from the sea, but this season the catch is modest, and survivors of Iskaal, a village to the east sacked by pirate slavers, keep pouring in. A gondola called the Ancient Lift climbs from the isle to the bluffs, and a great sea turtle carries travelers to Moa'ki Harbor in the Dragonblight.
sources: quest 11456 description (fish catch modest; Iskaal survivors)
warcraft.wiki.gg/wiki/Kamagua (largest tuskarr village, Isle of Spears; turtle to Moa'ki Harbor)
quest 11469 (Big Roy is killed for soap by the player during the pirate chain; not told)
notes: Checked: Big Roy boiled down for deck soap removed from the opening: it is the outcome of 11469, which the infiltrator does at Scalawag Point, and 11472 (Anuniaq) is offered only after it, so an arriving character cannot know it. Otherwise verified. Writer: AREA 3988. Opening only.

title: Scalawag Point
body: Scalawag Point, on Garvan's Reef at the southwestern edge of the fjord, is the den of the Northsea Freebooters. Their ships lie at anchor, duelists fight for wagers under Taruk's eye, and the witch doctor Zeh'gehn, whose speech only one or two can follow, divines traitors for the crew. Their captain, Mad Jonah Sterling, keeps to a cave west of the point and has set his crews raiding the Horde and Alliance fleets at once, and selling tuskarr as slaves, though the tuskarr die within days of leaving the cold.

parts.body: An outsider in pirate disguise, vouched for by a goblin, has been working up through the crew. Zeh'gehn's croaker named the rat among them: Crowleg Dan, who boasted that he had joined the Southsea pirates before he was cut down. Handsome Terry mourned an old friend who also owed him money.
sources: quest 11509 (Grezzix's cabin boy brings you in)

parts.body: Annie Bonn, the crew's second in command, then made her own move. She had Jonah Sterling killed in his hideout and, as word of his death spread, took the Freebooters for herself, promising to end their attacks on the infiltrator's allies, and hoping no one would learn she had arranged it.

sources: quest 11463 description (Northsea Freebooters at Scalawag Point on Garvan's Reef)
quest 11473 description (Zeh'gehn, witch doctor; only one or two understand him)
quest 11471 description (attacking both fleets; tuskarr die days after leaving)
notes: Checked: verified. Writer: AREA 3990 and 3989 (Garvan's Reef). Parts on DONE 11479 and DONE 11471 (neutral chain begun through Grezzix's disguise, 11509). Annie Bonn's gossip (npc_text 12187) names Jonah's death, so TALK on her is not used. spell_area 44018 in 3990 is not a phase (no phased spawns).

title: Vice Admiral Keller
body: Vice Admiral Keller commands Valgarde, and he means to hold it. A man with a wife and three children back in Elwynn, he knows that if the port falls the Alliance loses its main supply line into Northrend, and he would rather die fighting than serve the Lich King. His people built the town with their own hands, he says, and have no plans ever to give it up. Not everyone admires him: at Westguard Keep, Captain Adams resents how many soldiers Keller kept at Valgarde and calls him an insufferable egomaniac.

parts.body: When the vrykul harpooned his scouts and left them for dead in the forest, Keller saw it for what it was, a savage display meant to send Valgarde running in fear. It failed, he declared, and he turned the town from defense to attack, set on showing the giants what it means to make war on the Alliance.

sources: quest 11243 description (wife and three kids in Elwynn; primary supply line)
notes: Checked: verified. Writer: Faction 1: TALK on an Alliance NPC and Alliance-only quests. Part 1 on DONE 11244.

title: Captain Adams
body: Captain Adams, a dwarf of action with a famous temper, commands Westguard Keep. His orders are to hold the keep and garrison Fort Wildervar for the march into the Grizzly Hills, and he has too few soldiers for both, a shortage he lays at Vice Admiral Keller's feet. He sees threats on every side, from the burning Ember Clutch to the vrykul of Skorn and Gjalerbron and the Forsaken at Halgrind, and meets each of them head on. His advisor, Mage-Lieutenant Malister, quietly tries to temper his orders, with little success.
sources: quest 11187 reward text (Malister: tried to dissuade the captain; a dwarf of action)
quest 11291 request text (it sure wasn't because of Keller)
notes: Checked: verified. Writer: Faction 1. ACCEPT 11157 (his first quest, no prerequisite) and DONE 11291 (Keller's plans delivered). No parts: his campaigns are told in the place and story entries.

title: High Executor Anselm
body: High Executor Anselm commands Vengeance Landing. He has served in the military all his life, in many wars under many banners, but always in other people's battles. Not this time: every Forsaken soldier at the landing has come for one reason, to see Arthas killed, and the Alliance are merely an obstacle to be crushed on the way. He prizes discipline over heroics and has little patience for arrogant newcomers in shiny armor who think themselves above the chain of command.

parts.body: A dragonskin map, sniffed out by the landing's plaguehounds, showed him what he faced: Dragonflayer and Winterskorn villages around the fjord, and Vengeance Landing marked for death with a great skull. Forsaken records showed no sign of the vrykul in their lands for centuries, yet here they were just as the Forsaken moved against Arthas, and Anselm resolved to strike first, at Baleheim.
sources: quests 11227 and 11253 descriptions (plaguehounds to sniff out enemy scouts; the hound leads to the scroll)
quest 11270 reward text (arrogant fool in shiny armor; chain of command)
notes: Checked: part 1 'carried by vrykul scouts' unsupported (11253 has a plaguehound lead to the scroll); now sniffed out by the landing's plaguehounds. Otherwise verified. Writer: Faction 2: Horde NPC and Horde-only quests. Part 1 on ACCEPT 11295 (its description tells the centuries; the map's reading is the reward text of 11254, which must be turned in first). Keleseth's visit is in 49531 part 3.

title: Thoralius the Wise
body: Thoralius the Wise is a draenei seer at Valgarde. The Explorers' League may dig up pieces of the past, he says, and the vice admiral may wring knowledge of the present out of his enemies by force, but the truth lies with the spirits. With the proper reagents, burned in his incense and breathed in, he can look into the spirit world, where he holds that the past, present and future of Northrend reside. His reagent pouch, unfortunately, went down with a ship in Daggercap Bay.

parts.body: With his pouch recovered he breathed the smoke and saw something that left him shaking. The spirit world, he says, has fallen under the sway of the Lich King: val'kyr, creatures of pure nightmare, now stand watch over the realm of the elements, guarding a terrible secret at Wyrmskull.

In the spirit world at Wyrmskull stood a vrykul couple of long ago over a newborn child, which they took as a sign that they too were cursed. The father would be rid of it before King Ymiron learned of it, the mother begged to hide it somewhere far away, and Thoralius could not see why these ancient figures looked like the vrykul now attacking Valgarde.

The visions reached back fifteen thousand years. At Nifflevar the spirits showed Ymiron blaming the titans for cursing his people with malformed children, renouncing the old gods and decreeing that every such infant die at birth. The children, Thoralius concluded, were human. There was no extinct missing link: the vrykul are the progenitors of humanity.
sources: quest 11344 description (visions dating back 15,000 years) and reward text
creature_text 23975 (Fire grant me vision; inhales the smoke)
notes: Checked: phasing confirmed. The spirit world is not a spell_area phase: each Incense Burner (items 33637 and 33774, given with 11343 and 11344) casts Echo of Ymiron (42786/43466: phase aura, phase 2), which shows the phase 2 spawns; the ancient couple's script (24314, actionlist 2431400) speaks creature_text 24314/24315 to whoever comes near and casts the 11343 credit (43458), and Ymiron's script (24321, actionlist 2432100) speaks his decree and casts the 11344 credit (43468). So part 2's lines are shown on the way to DONE 11343 and part 3's on the way to DONE 11344. Part 2 checked line by line against creature_text 24314/24315 and the 11343 reward text. Part 1 on ACCEPT 11343 (description). Thoralius named a draenei (display 21947). Writer: Faction 1: Alliance quests (11333, 11343, 11344 AllowableRaces 1101; 11343/11344 also hidden from Horde by his faction). The visions are the phase 2 spirit world (Ancient Male and Female Vrykul 24314/24315 at Wyrmskull, King Ymiron 24321 at Nifflevar), seen only while 11343/11344 are active, so told on their DONE.

title: Chieftain Ashtotem
body: Chieftain Ashtotem leads the taunka of Camp Winterhoof. He speaks plainly to outsiders: among his people trust is earned, not given. The dead walk the land and even arrive on ships from across the great ocean, the vrykul have woken in their fortresses, and he has decided that his people must leave for safer lands to the north, though some of his warriors would rather stand and fight. Until the camp departs he accepts any help with its preparations, and sends what fighters he can against the vrykul of Skorn and Gjalerbron.
sources: quest 11411 reward text (trust is earned, not given)
notes: Checked: verified. Writer: Faction 2: the Horde reaches him through 11411 or 12566 (one exclusive group), and only the Horde takes his quests. No parts.

title: Queen Angerboda
body: Angerboda is queen of the vrykul and wife of King Ymiron, who lies dormant in the Winter's Terrace at the northern end of Gjalerbron. With necrolords of the Scourge at her side she drives a ritual to wake him, demanding ever more sacrifices and calling on her husband-king to rise and reign again with the might of the Lich King behind him. Her patience is wearing thin: the ritual moves too slowly, and the help the Scourge promised has not sped it.

parts.body: Queen Angerboda fell in the Winter's Terrace, cut down beside the sleeping husband she had labored so long to wake, and her calls for more sacrifices fell silent at last.
sources: creature 24023 Queen Angerboda (guid 42162, map 571, phase 1, 150 second respawn; posarea 4065)
smart_scripts 24023 (on death summons the Lich King 29394)
creature_text 24023 group 2 (yells: more sacrifices; my husband-king will awaken; with the might of the Lich King; your master promised)
creature 24023 and 29393 King Ymiron at Gjalerhorn (posarea 4065)
notes: Checked: KILL 24023 kept: she is a fixed open-world spawn (one creature row, phase 1, respawn 150 s), not a quest summon. Part 1 trimmed: 'before the king could open his eyes' dropped, since on her death the Lich King (29394, summoned by her SmartAI) appears, yells that Ymiron will serve him in Utgarde Pinnacle and teleports Ymiron away, which a bystander sees; that is told on DONE 11452/11453 in 49533 part 3 (their reward text tells it too), so the part now says only that she fell. Writer: AREA 4065 (Gjalerhorn, where she and Ymiron stand) and ACCEPT 11452/11453 (Alliance and Horde). Part 1 is a KILL and tells only her fall: whether the Lich King's arrival is visible to bystanders is not confirmed in the database, so it is told only on DONE 11452/11453 in 49533.

title: Elder Atuik
body: Elder Atuik is chieftain of the Kalu'ak of Kamagua. His people are peaceful and live mainly from the sea, hunting on land only in times of great need, and this is such a time, for pirates have sacked the nearby village of Iskaal and its survivors keep arriving. Atuik remembers the tales of Issliruk, the spirit of war, a silver eagle who fought a hundred worgs to save his young, and he is ready to set the old peace aside to defend his kin.

parts.body: The slavers who raided Iskaal had lost their minds and slaughtered all their captives. With spear tips carved from chimaera horn and the totem of Issliruk raised, Atuik sent help to Iskaal to cut them down, and the Kalu'ak swore themselves forever in their avengers' debt.

notes: Checked: verified. Writer: Faction 0: Kalu'ak (1950) are neutral, and 11456 is open to both factions. Part 1 on DONE 11458.

title: Valgarde Besieged
body: Newcomers to Valgarde are greeted by the dwarf Macalroy, who doubts the green recruits Fordragon sent can hold the port much longer and sends anyone better equipped on to Vice Admiral Keller. Keller lays it out plainly: if Valgarde falls, the Alliance loses its main supply line into Northrend. The town had stood a month when malformed giants appeared as if from thin air. An archaeology team was lost, townsfolk were dragged away to the ruins to the north, and the defenders at the gate face wave after wave of raiders and their worgs.

parts.body: The soldiers rescued from Wyrmskull Village gave the enemy a name. The giants call themselves vrykul, and the tribe that has taken the village answers to a mystic named Yanis, himself the underling of another vrykul, Ingvar the Plunderer.

From Yanis's cave came the Dragonflayer battle plans. They showed the fjord dotted with vrykul villages and a different tribe readying an assault on Westguard Keep, which had not been heard from in days. Keller sent the plans west by gryphon to warn Captain Adams.

Scout Valory's search of Wyrmskull found nearly everyone slain or taken. On the hill above, Defender Mordun stood among the bodies of his best men. The vrykul, he warned, are fearless and yearn for a death in battle, but there is one they esteem, Ingvar, and bringing him down might break their spirit.

sources: quest 11243 description and objectives (Dragonflayer Invaders, Worgs)
notes: Checked: verified. Writer: Faction 1: Alliance chain 11228, 11243, 11244, 11255, 11290, 11291, 11251. Bolvar named only as the one who sent the recruits (no entry). Mordun's 11252 (Utgarde Keep) used only as a source; part 3 is on DONE 11251, whose turn-in to Mordun offers it.

title: The Wyrmskull Tablets
body: Beltrand McSorf of the Explorers' League was the only one of his crew to make it back to Valgarde when the monsters struck their dig at Wyrmskull. The team had been on the brink of an archaeological breakthrough, and he will not give it up: the artifacts they uncovered must be found, and any of his crew who might still be alive with them. The ruins now lie in the hands of the Dragonflayer vrykul, and McSorf asks anyone bound that way to look first for Pulroy, the last of his team he saw.

parts.body: Pulroy was found dead with his journal clutched in his hand, and Zedd dead too, about to be fed to the worgs. Glorenfeld still lived in the Utgarde Catacombs, but Daegarn had been taken deeper by the Dragonflayer chieftain as a sacrifice to the Dread King, with the cipher for the tablets hidden in his beard, as dwarves do.

The vrykul had searched the beard first. The cipher had passed to Oluf the Violent, chieftain of the gladiators, and only by beating his fighters in the Ring of Judgement could he be drawn out and the cipher won back. Glorenfeld puzzled for a moment over Daegarn's talk of something judging the bouts, then counted the cost: tablets and cipher recovered, two dwarves dead.

McSorf's first look at the tablets suggested that whatever once lived at Wyrmskull was an ancestor of humankind, perhaps wiped out by the vrykul. Unable to read them even with the cipher, he sent everything on to the League's cryptographer, Stanwad, at the outpost on the southeastern bluffs.

Stanwad was not impressed. After all the lives spent to recover it, the great discovery turned out to be an ancient recipe for tundra stew: pictures of common vegetables beside a mouth chewing on them, a code no one needed a cipher to break.

notes: Checked: verified. Writer: Faction 1: Alliance chain 11273, 11274, 11276, 11277, 11299, 11300, 11278, 11448. The Ring of Judgement and the catacombs are told as places in 49502.

title: The Last of the North Fleet
body: The Forsaken have destroyed the Alliance's easternmost fleet, but the survivors of Stormwind's North Fleet have barricaded themselves on the Derelict Strand south of Vengeance Landing and held out far longer than anyone expected. High Executor Anselm wants it finished. In the lands of the Lich King the dead are a weapon that may rise at any moment, so the corpses west of the town are put to the torch, and his officers in the field, Dark Ranger Lyana and Deathstalker Razael, are pressed for their reports.

parts.body: The cannons on the strand kept the Forsaken at bay, so orders went to Captain Harker's ships offshore, the Windrunner, the Queen's Reprisal and the Oblivion, to silence them. Approaching through the reefs, the ships were themselves boarded by North Fleet marines and had to be won back before their guns could fire.

Smoke flares marked the cannons on the northern wall, the ships' guns cleared the way, and Lyana's troops advanced. In the confusion the Alliance leaders, Captain Olster, Lieutenant Celeyne and Sergeant Lorric, were hunted down behind their own lines, and Lyana declared the victory beyond dispute.

Anselm had no time to celebrate. Prince Keleseth of the San'layn came to the landing with an offer from Arthas: abandon Sylvanas's childish rebellion and command armies far greater, or be driven out by the vrykul, who had cast their lot with the Lich King. Anselm answered with his archers. The prince shrugged off the volley, drank in the souls of the dying and vowed to return once Utgarde's armies had fallen upon the landing.
sources: quest 11234 reward text (visitors from the west)

notes: Checked: part 3 confirmed: smart_scripts 23780 event 20 (quest 11234 rewarded) runs actionlist 2378000, which summons Prince Keleseth 24041 (subname The San'layn, shown to anyone), plays creature_text 23780 groups 0-3 and 24041 groups 0-7, has the archers fire and Keleseth teleport, drain souls and despawn. The part tells only those lines; 'return with Utgarde's armies' brought closer to his last line (return after Utgarde's armies descend). Writer: Faction 2: Horde chain 11270, 11221, 11229, 11230, 11232, 11233, 11234. Part 3 on DONE 11234: SmartAI 23780 runs actionlist 2378000 on its reward (Prince Keleseth 24041 is summoned and speaks creature_text 24041 groups 0-7; Anselm's archers fire). Keleseth has a death-knight-only entry in the Scarlet Enclave and is an Utgarde Keep boss, so he gets no entry here. A Score to Settle (11272) is an instance quest and is not used.

title: The New Plague
body: Ever since Arthas condemned them to undeath, the Royal Apothecary Society has worked on a plague of its own, one meant to devour all flesh, living, dead or undead, and the apothecaries have brought it to Northrend to deliver to the Scourge's doorstep. Not everything has gone to plan: the Alliance intercepted a ship carrying their latest strain, and the strains sent from the Undercity keep failing. At Westguard Keep, meanwhile, scouts report the Forsaken up to something at the Dragonflayer village of Halgrind.

parts.body: Apothecary Lysander's strain went on from Vengeance Landing to New Agamand, where Chief Plaguebringer Harris brewed a version made for vrykul from the blood of Thorvald, Halgrind's fled chieftain. Sprayed on the plagued villagers, it did not melt them as he had hoped, but it turned them against one another, and Harris, ever practical, declared the research a success.

After what he called an eternity of failure, Chief Plaguebringer Harris of New Agamand announced perfection at last: a strain to tear down the very fabric of life. It had no proper name yet, so he called it blight, and sent a specimen by bat to Venomspite in the Dragonblight.

Scout Knowles found the Forsaken spraying plague on Halgrind's vrykul and recovered an apothecary's package from the village. At the keep the tipsy amateur alchemist Peppy Wrongnozzle mixed it into a vaccine and tried it on a vrykul prisoner, who melted. She feared she had perfected the plague for the Forsaken, and Captain Adams heard the news in disgust.

Adams would not let a Forsaken super plague melt his soldiers where they stood. A gryphon rider loaded with bombs flew over New Agamand and blew its plague tanks to smithereens, and the gleeful captain declared it a lesson for the Forsaken.

sources: creature_text 24126 group 6 (strains from Undercity keep failing)
notes: Checked: read as each faction. Horde: opening, then parts 1-2; Alliance: opening, then parts 3-4; each side reads on cleanly. The opening's 'the long voyage seems to weaken what arrives' came from 11168, a later quest, and is replaced by Lysander's complaint that the Undercity strains keep failing (creature_text 24126). Part 1 now names Lysander and Vengeance Landing; part 2 names Harris in full, since 12181 has no prerequisite and can be earned without part 1. Part 2 names Venomspite only as 12181's destination; nothing of the Wrathgate, and 12182 stays unused. Writer: Faction 0: Horde parts 1-2 (Lysander, Harris), Alliance parts 3-4 (Knowles, Peppy, Adams). Each faction's parts read on from the opening. Told only as these quests show it: no Wrathgate, no Putress, nothing of the Undercity; Venomspite is named only as where the specimen is sent (12182 To Venomspite is Dragonblight's and not used).

title: The Slumbering King
body: Word from the north troubles Westguard Keep and Camp Winterhoof alike. At Gjalerbron, the great fortress of the vrykul in the north of the fjord, the giants have woken and are performing an awakening ritual fed by living sacrifices kept in cages. Captain Adams and Chieftain Ashtotem each send fighters to cull the vrykul before they finish whatever they are doing, while Father Levariol and Greatmother Ankha plead for the prisoners to be freed, whoever they are, lest the ritual wake something even more evil.

parts.body: The Scourge is at Gjalerbron too. Necromancers work beside the vrykul, plainly meaning to bring them into the Lich King's fold, under a leader called Necro Overlord Mezhen, who keeps to a platform at the rear of the fortress.

Plans taken from the vrykul revealed an attack to be led by the frost wyrm Glacion, which circles overhead, at the command of Wyrmcaller Vile. Blowing the wyrmcaller's own horn called the beast down to its death, and the horn was carried away so it could never fall into the wrong hands again.

Papers dropped by Mezhen told what the ritual was for. Queen Angerboda was struggling to wake her husband, King Ymiron, in the Winter's Terrace. She was slain there, but the Lich King himself carried Ymiron off, which no one liked the sound of. Still, the vrykul plans had taken a heavy blow, and time had been bought.

notes: Checked: verified. Writer: Faction 0: Alliance 11235, 11231, 11236, 11237/11238, 11452; Horde 11263, 11265, 11264, 11266/11267, 11453. Part 3 tells the Lich King carrying off Ymiron, as 11452/11453 reward text says; nothing of Utgarde Pinnacle.

title: The Relics of Shield Hill
body: Tuskarr hunters returning to Kamagua swear that the dead have risen along an old hunting trail by Shield Hill, an ancient vrykul burial ground on the bluffs, and are out for blood. Elder Atuik sent Orfus of Kamagua, one of his strongest warriors, with Lunk-tusk to find out why. The undead attacked them as they neared the graves, and the two were parted. Now Orfus waits at the Ancient Lift for anyone brave enough to search the desecrated graves for clues.

parts.body: The clues pointed to pirates. The Northsea Freebooters had plundered the burial mounds, and Orfus resolved to recover what they had stolen and return it to the graves, so that the spirits might rest and his people know peace once more.
sources: quest 11507 description (war with the Northsea Freebooters, shown as 11504 is turned in)

parts.body: The goblin Grezzix, who smuggled Orfus's champion into Scalawag Point, wanted nothing to do with the relics, and inside, Silvermoon Harry warned that everyone who had touched them was now dead, missing or both. The pirates were plainly afraid of what they had taken.

All four relics were recovered, from a derelict ship, a Forsaken destroyer, a crew of ghosts and a madman's den, and laid back in the mounds: the Frozen Heart of Isuldof, the Shield of the Aesirites, the Staff of Storm's Fury and the Ancient Armor of the Kvaldir. It came too late. The dead warned that the Kvaldir return out of the mist and fog, and Orfus feared they would show the Kalu'ak no mercy.
Elder Atuik took the warning gravely. The Kalu'ak of Kamagua now prepare for battle and send word to their kin across the sea of what is coming, hoping it is not already too late.

sources: quest 11507 reward text (one of our strongest warriors)
notes: Checked: title changed from 'The Kvaldir Relics': the Kvaldir are named only by the spirits at the mounds during 11568 (part 3), so the title gave that away to anyone who had just accepted 11504. Part 1's source corrected (creature_text 24874-24877 is spoken during 11568; the Freebooters are named by 11507, offered on 11504's turn-in). Both sides reach the opening: ACCEPT 11504 is open to all races at Orfus, ACCEPT 11573 is the Alliance lead-in. 11568 requires 11511, 11512 and 11567 (NextQuestID 11568, exclusive group -11511), so part 3's four relics hold. Writer: Faction 0: 11504 onward are open to both; 11573 is an Alliance lead-in from Westguard. Shield Hill (4057) gets no place entry; it is told here. The Kvaldir quests of Hrothgar's Landing are not touched; this is the Howling Fjord's own chain.

title: The Iron Dwarves
body: Strange dwarves of living iron have appeared in the eastern fjord. At Giants' Run, a rocky plateau southeast of Fort Wildervar, iron rune stonecallers and binders coax stone giants out of the ground and carve runes into them, as if to make them into weapons. On the high bluffs farther south they have driven the Explorers' League from its dig sites at Ivald's Ruin and Baelgun's Excavation Site, and rather than digging up the relics there, they are burying them, as though no one must ever find what lies below.

parts.body: The runes drove the giants north and west toward a lodestone the binders had made: Megalith, the mightiest of the runed giants, created by Binder Murdis to lead them. Megalith was felled in the foothills of Frostblade Peak, and with his last breath urged his brethren to let nothing keep them from the Stoneforge, a name no one knew, though it sounded like something of the titans.

Walt of the Explorers' League built a false iron construct to slip back into Baelgun's. Sent into a thundering cave around a titan statue, it brought back word that the iron dwarves are at work in the Storm Peaks, along with a name Walt had never heard: Loken. He sent the news on to the League's base in the Dragonblight.

sources: quest 11346 description (Giants' Run southeast; coaxing giants; carving runes; weapons)
quest 11474 description and reward text (pushed out of Ivald's Ruin and Baelgun's; burying the sites)
notes: Checked: part 2 kept to the 11495 reward text, which only asks what the iron dwarves are doing in the Storm Peaks and what Loken is; 'speak of a being called Loken' made a name Walt had never heard. Loken and the Storm Peaks stay hooks for the Storm Peaks. Writer: Faction 0: Giants' Run chains for both (11346-11359 Alliance, 11350-11367 Horde); the Explorers' League chain is Alliance (part 2). Loken and the Storm Peaks are named only as the reward text names them; their story belongs to the Storm Peaks.
